description: Additional date and time functionality: relative dates (Today, Tomorrow), Unix and Julian time conversion, date predicates and selection, calendars and time zones, session timing, plus the astronomical date functions (sunrise/sunset, moon phase, sun and moon positions, sidereal time).

tools.name: Today
tools.description: Today gives the current date as a day-granularity DateObject; Tomorrow and Yesterday give the adjacent days. They are the natural anchors for DateRange, DatePlus and Between filters and, unlike Now, carry no time-of-day component.
tools.example:
DateRange[Today, DatePlus[Today, 7]]
DateDifference[DateObject[{2024, 1, 1}], Today, "Day"]
Select[records, Between[#date, {Yesterday, Today}] &]
tools.notes: Today is re-evaluated every time it is used; store it in a variable for consistency inside a long computation.

tools.name: UnixTime
tools.description: Converts a date to seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00 UTC (the Unix epoch) and FromUnixTime converts back to a DateObject; UnixTime[] gives the current time. Use them to exchange timestamps with databases, JSON APIs and log files.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: DateObject, date list or date string.

parameters.name: secs
parameters.description: Seconds since the epoch (integer or real; milliseconds must be divided by 1000).

tools.name: JulianDate
tools.description: Gives the Julian date (days since noon on 1 January 4713 BC) of a date, the time scale used in astronomy; FromJulianDate converts back. Also supports "ModifiedJulianDate" and other variants.

parameters.name: jd
parameters.description: Julian date as a real number.

tools.name: FromAbsoluteTime
tools.description: Converts an absolute time (seconds since 1 January 1900, as returned by AbsoluteTime) into a DateObject, optionally in a given time zone. Pair it with AbsoluteTime for fast arithmetic on large date lists.

parameters.name: secs
parameters.description: Seconds since 1900-01-01 00:00 in the local time zone.

tools.name: FromDateString
tools.description: Parses a date string into a DateObject using an explicit format specification (the same element names as DateString: "Year", "Month", "Day", "Hour24" ...), which is faster and more predictable than DateObject["string"] for known formats.

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: List of DateString elements and literal separators, or a named format.

tools.notes: Introduced in 13.0. DateObject["string"] and Interpreter["Date"] guess formats heuristically; DatePattern builds string patterns for dates.

tools.name: DateObjectQ
tools.description: Tests whether an expression is a valid DateObject (and TimeObjectQ a TimeObject). Use them to validate parsed input before date arithmetic, since DateObject["bad string"] returns an unevaluated or failed object.
tools.example:
DateObjectQ[DateObject["2024-02-30"]] (* False: invalid date *)
Select[parsed, DateObjectQ]

tools.name: DateWithinQ
tools.description: DateWithinQ[d1, d2] tests whether date d2 lies within the span of the coarser date d1 (e.g. a day within a month); DateOverlapsQ tests whether two date spans or intervals overlap. Both understand DateObject granularity (Year, Month, Week, Day) and DateInterval.

parameters.name: d1, d2
parameters.description: DateObjects with possibly different granularity, or DateIntervals.

tools.example:
DateWithinQ[DateObject[{2024, 5}], DateObject[{2024, 5, 17}]] (* True *)
DateOverlapsQ[DateInterval[{d1, d2}], DateInterval[{d3, d4}]]

tools.name: DateSelect
tools.description: Selects the dates in a list (or the elements of a DateRange) satisfying a criterion such as BusinessDayQ, a weekday name, or a custom predicate. Convenient for generating schedules (all Mondays, all business days) from a date range.
tools.usage:
DateSelect[{d1, d2, ...}, crit]
DateSelect[{start, end}, crit]
DateSelect[{start, end}, crit, incr]

parameters.name: crit
parameters.description: Predicate function or a day specification such as Monday, "Weekend", "BusinessDay".

tools.name: CalendarConvert
tools.description: Converts a DateObject to another calendar system ("Gregorian", "Julian", "Islamic", "Hebrew", "Chinese", "Jewish", "Persian", ...), returning a DateObject with CalendarType set; CalendarData gives calendar properties. Use it for historical dates and for religious/civil calendars in scheduling.
tools.usage:
CalendarConvert[date, "Calendar"]
CalendarData["Calendar", "prop"]
DateObject[{y, m, d}, CalendarType -> "Hebrew"]

tools.name: TimeZoneOffset
tools.description: Gives the offset in hours of a time zone from UTC (or between two zones) at a given date, taking daylight-saving rules into account; TimeZone is the option (and DateObject element) naming the zone, either as a number or an IANA name such as "America/New_York". $SystemTimeZone is the OS zone and $TimeZoneEntity the entity form.
tools.usage:
TimeZoneOffset[]
TimeZoneOffset[tz]
TimeZoneOffset[tz, date]
TimeZoneOffset[tz1, tz2, date]
DateObject[{2024, 7, 1, 12}, TimeZone -> "Europe/Berlin"]

parameters.name: tz
parameters.description: Numeric offset, IANA zone string or TimeZone entity.

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Date at which the offset is evaluated (DST-aware).

tools.name: LocalTime
tools.description: LocalTime[loc] gives the current time at a geographic location (city entity, GeoPosition, time zone) and LocalTimeZone[loc] its time zone. Use them to display world clocks and to localize timestamps to where data was recorded.

parameters.name: loc
parameters.description: Entity["City", ...], GeoPosition, country or time zone specification.

tools.name: $DateStringFormat
tools.description: The default format used by DateString and by the display of DateObject when no explicit format is given (a list of elements such as {"DateTimeShort"}); DateFormat is the corresponding option of DateObject and DateListPlot. Set $DateStringFormat to standardise output (e.g. ISO 8601) across a session or script.

tools.name: SessionTime
tools.description: SessionTime[] gives the seconds elapsed since the kernel session started, TimeUsed[] the CPU seconds consumed by the kernel, and Clock[] a dynamically updating time value for animations. Use SessionTime for coarse wall-clock stamps and TimeUsed for CPU-bound profiling without AbsoluteTiming wrappers.
tools.usage:
SessionTime[]
TimeUsed[]
Clock[]
Clock[{min, max}, t]

parameters.name: {min, max}
parameters.description: Clock range cycled over period t seconds.

tools.example:
t0 = TimeUsed[]; result = heavy[]; Print["CPU s: ", TimeUsed[] - t0]
Dynamic[Graphics[{Disk[{Cos[Clock[2 Pi]], Sin[Clock[2 Pi]]}, 0.1]}, PlotRange -> 1.2]]

tools.name: CurrentDate
tools.description: CurrentDate[granularity] gives the current date at a chosen granularity ("Week", "Month", "Quarter", "Year", ...), while NextDate and PreviousDate give the next/previous unit or named day (e.g. NextDate["Monday"], PreviousDate["Quarter"]). They simplify period-based scheduling and reporting.
tools.example:
CurrentDate["Quarter"]
DateRange[PreviousDate["Month"], CurrentDate["Month"], "Day"] (* last month's days *)
NextDate[Today, "Friday"]

tools.name: MinDate
tools.description: MinDate, MaxDate and MidDate give the earliest, latest and middle date of a list of dates or a DateInterval; Min/Max also work on dates but these handle intervals and mixed granularity. Use them to compute the span of a dataset.
tools.usage:
MinDate[{d1, d2, ...}]
MaxDate[{d1, d2, ...}]
MidDate[{d1, d2, ...}]
MinDate[dateInterval]

parameters.name: dates
parameters.description: List of DateObjects or a DateInterval.

tools.name: InfiniteFuture
tools.description: InfiniteFuture and InfinitePast are symbolic dates later/earlier than every date, useful as sentinels in DateInterval, Between filters and sorting (e.g. an open-ended validity period).
tools.example:
valid = DateInterval[{DateObject[{2024, 1, 1}], InfiniteFuture}];
DateWithinQ[valid, Today] (* True *)

tools.name: ConformDates
tools.description: Converts a list of dates given in mixed forms (strings, lists, DateObjects, absolute times) to a uniform representation, typically DateObjects with the same granularity and time zone. Use it to clean imported timestamp columns before TimeSeries or DateListPlot.

tools.name: DayRound
tools.description: Rounds a date to the nearest day matching a specification (business day, weekend, named weekday), moving forward or backward as requested ("Nearest", "Previous", "Next"). Used for settlement-date and deadline calculations.
tools.example:
DayRound[DateObject[{2024, 5, 4}], "BusinessDay"] (* Friday 3 May or Monday 6 May depending on nearest *)
DayRound[deadline, "BusinessDay", "Next"]

tools.name: DatePattern
tools.description: DatePattern[{elem1, elem2, ...}] is a string pattern matching dates written with the given DateString elements and separators; use it in StringCases to find and extract dates embedded in free text, then convert with DateObject.
tools.usage:
StringCases[text, DatePattern[{"Year", "-", "Month", "-", "Day"}]]
StringCases[text, d : DatePattern[{"Day", " ", "MonthName", " ", "Year"}] :> DateObject[d]]

parameters.name: elems
parameters.description: DateString element names and literal separators.

tools.name: Duration
tools.description: Gives the length of a DateInterval, TimeSeries, Audio, Video or other time-spanning object as a Quantity of time. For two dates use DateDifference; for objects Duration is the uniform accessor.

parameters.name: obj
parameters.description: DateInterval, TimeSeries, Audio, Video, DateObject (of coarse granularity).

tools.name: LeapYearQ
tools.description: Tests whether a date (or year) falls in a leap year, for any supported calendar; DaylightQ tests whether daylight-saving time is in effect at a date and location. Small but frequently needed calendar predicates.

tools.name: Sunrise
tools.description: Gives the sunrise (Sunset the sunset) time as a DateObject for the current or given location and date, using the built-in astronomical ephemeris; options include the definition of horizon/twilight ("CivilTwilight", etc.). Use them for solar-energy, photography and scheduling calculations.
tools.usage:
Sunrise[]
Sunrise[date]
Sunrise[loc, date]
Sunset[loc, date]
Sunrise[loc, date, "CivilTwilight"]
tools.example:
{Sunrise[Here, Today], Sunset[Here, Today]}
DateDifference[Sunrise[loc, d], Sunset[loc, d], "Hour"] (* day length *)

tools.name: SunPosition
tools.description: Gives the position of the Sun in the sky (azimuth and altitude by default, or equatorial/ecliptic coordinates) for a location and date; MoonPosition does the same for the Moon. Both accept lists of dates for producing sun-path diagrams and solar-panel orientation studies.
tools.usage:
SunPosition[]
SunPosition[loc, date]
SunPosition[loc, date, "Equatorial"]
MoonPosition[loc, date]

tools.name: MoonPhase
tools.description: Gives the phase of the Moon at a date as an illuminated fraction, or with "Name" ("FullMoon", "WaxingCrescent", ...) or "Icon" forms; also works for lists of dates. Use it for calendars, tide models and astronomy visualisations.

tools.name: SiderealTime
tools.description: Gives the local (or Greenwich) sidereal time at a location and date as a time Quantity, needed to convert between equatorial and horizon coordinates in telescope pointing and astrophotography.

tools.name: AstroPosition
tools.description: Represents a position on the celestial sphere in a given reference frame ("Equatorial", "Horizon", "Ecliptic", "Galactic") - the astronomical analogue of GeoPosition - and converts between frames given a location and date. Used with AstroGraphics for sky maps and with AstroDistance/AstroAngularSeparation.
tools.usage:
AstroPosition[{ra, dec}]
AstroPosition[{az, alt}, "Horizon"]
AstroPosition[Entity["Star", "Sirius"]]
AstroPosition[pos, {"Horizon", loc, date}]

parameters.name: {c1, c2}
parameters.description: Coordinates in the frame (degrees or Quantities).

tools.notes: Introduced in 13.1 together with AstroGraphics; AstronomicalData/PlanetData provide the underlying ephemerides.

tools.name: SolarEclipse
tools.description: Gives the date (and, with properties, the type, path and magnitude) of the next or previous solar eclipse after a date; LunarEclipse does the same for lunar eclipses. Use with GeoGraphics to plot eclipse paths.
tools.usage:
SolarEclipse[]
SolarEclipse[date]
SolarEclipse[date, "Type"]
SolarEclipse[{d1, d2}, All]
LunarEclipse[date, "MaximumEclipseDate"]

parameters.name: date
parameters.description: Reference date; the next eclipse after it is returned.

tools.name: TimeSystemConvert
tools.description: Converts a date between time systems such as "UTC", "TAI", "TT" (Terrestrial Time), "TDB", "GPS" and "UT1", which differ by leap seconds and relativistic corrections; TimeSystem is the corresponding DateObject option. Needed for precise astronomical and satellite calculations.
tools.example: TimeSystemConvert[DateObject[{2024, 1, 1, 0, 0, 0}, TimeZone -> 0], "TAI"] (* 37 s ahead of UTC *)

tools.name: DateTicksFormat
tools.description: Option of DateListPlot, DateHistogram, TimelinePlot and other date-axis plots specifying how tick labels are formatted, using DateString elements such as {"MonthNameShort", " ", "Year"}; combine with PlotRange given as DateObjects to control the visible date window and with DateFunction to preprocess date values.
tools.usage:
DateListPlot[ts, DateTicksFormat -> {"MonthNameShort", " ", "Year"}]
DateListPlot[ts, PlotRange -> {{DateObject[{2024, 1, 1}], DateObject[{2024, 6, 30}]}, Automatic}]
